extracted.intended_audience: researchers, academics, and policymakers studying agricultural cooperatives and cooperative performance
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA-based systematic review framework for analyzing empirical studies of agricultural cooperatives, organizing each study by purpose, methodology, factors examined, and key findings to enable comparative analysis and guide future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PRISMA methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: This study presents a comprehensive review of existing literature on ACs using the PRISMA methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PRISMA for systematic identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion of studies; report search strategy, inclusion/exclusion criteria, screening flow (PRISMA flowchart), and transparent study selection so results are reproducible and comprehensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (study aim/objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each selected study was analyzed based on the study's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and record the explicit aims and research questions of each study to clarify why the study was conducted and to group studies by objective (e.g., performance evaluation, member participation, service delivery). Use purpose to interpret findings and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (research design and methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each selected study was analyzed based on methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document study design (qualitative, quantitative, mixed methods), sampling approach, data sources, measurement instruments, and analytical techniques. Evaluate methodological rigor and comparability across studies when synthesizing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors examined (variables and constructs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each selected study was analyzed based on factors examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the specific variables or constructs each study investigated (e.g., management practices, marketing strategies, workforce characteristics, education). Use consistent coding of factors so cross-study comparisons and categorizations are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key findings (main results and conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each selected study was analyzed based on key findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize main results, reported effect directions/strengths, and authors' conclusions. Capture contextual qualifiers and limitations to inform synthesis and to avoid overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize variables for comparative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: These variables were then categorized to enable a more robust comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create stable, coherent categories for purposes, methodologies, factors, and findings (coding scheme). Use those categories to aggregate evidence, identify patterns, and support meta-interpretation across heterogeneous studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess common drivers of cooperative success
rubrics_metrics.description: The review highlights that the success of ACs is driven by effective management, strong marketing strategies, and a dedicated workforce; education emerges as a critical factor, irrespective of age or gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or designing AC studies, prioritize measurement and analysis of management quality, marketing capacity, workforce commitment, and education/training. Treat these as primary explanatory factors to test and report on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for context-specificity of strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for success differ among cooperatives, underscoring the need for context-specific research to accurately assess the status and needs of ACs in various regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze and report contextual moderators (region, legal environment, cooperative size/type, commodity, socio-economic conditions). Avoid assuming universal applicability; explicitly consider and test how context alters relationships and recommended interventions.
